summary: Product-scoped record for Ndax's Canadian proof-of-stake service. Ndax launched its first flexible crypto staking program on 15 February 2022 and current first-party material documents continued multi-asset staking through third-party validators.
what_happened: Ndax announced on 15 February 2022 that its first flexible crypto staking program was available starting that day, initially supporting ETH, DOT and ADA. Current Ndax policy and relationship materials document opt-in staking, experienced third-party validator operators, network/protocol-dependent rewards, bonding and unbonding, redemption options, non-guaranteed rewards, slashing/on-chain risks and administration fees. Ndax's current User Agreement states users receive full rights, interests and title to Virtual Assets purchased on the platform and describes custody arrangements for assets left on-platform. CYA records those express terms without converting staking availability or security claims into a principal or insolvency guarantee.
uncertainty_notes: Current staking operation and 2022 launch are strongly supported. Reward rates, supported assets, bonding/unbonding and fees can change. CYA does not treat custody/security disclosures as a guarantee against protocol, validator, platform or insolvency risk.
notes: Ndax serves Canadian residents and current legal material describes title/custody safeguards for on-platform Virtual Assets. Staking-specific risks and third-party validator dependencies remain explicit.

summary: Product-scoped record for VALR's on-chain proof-of-stake service. VALR officially launched staking on 27 June 2023 with SOL and AVAX and current governing terms preserve account-holder ownership of staked assets while VALR facilitates protocol staking.
what_happened: VALR announced on 27 June 2023 that it had officially launched crypto staking, initially supporting SOL and AVAX. Current VALR Terms of Service document opt-in on-chain proof-of-stake staking, transfer of staked assets into a separate account for protocol facilitation, protocol-derived rewards, configurable commissions, unstaking delays and slashing risk. The same current terms explicitly state that rights, title and ownership of staked assets remain with the eligible account holder, that the assets are held for the account holder and are not VALR property, and that they are not subject to claims of VALR creditors. CYA preserves those express current terms while keeping market, validator, protocol and operational risk separate from ownership treatment.
uncertainty_notes: The 2023 launch and current staking terms are strongly supported. Supported assets, commissions, reward rates, unstaking timing and product presentation can change. Current ownership/creditor language is terms-version specific and should be reverified when terms change.
notes: VALR's current terms contain unusually explicit ownership and creditor-treatment language for staked assets. This does not eliminate protocol, validator, slashing, market or platform-operational risk.
